clue.text: Choose a flower, as you might say — something for the dining table

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the phrase becomes the name of a relish

parts.note: choose is PICK, and a flower is A LILY

explanation.surface: A gardener is told to pick a flower, perhaps for a vase on the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as you might say' tells you to say PICK A LILY aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Piccalilli is a mustard-and-vegetable pickle that gets served as a relish at meals.

clue.text: Fish glides along

definitions.meaning: a skate is a flat cartilaginous fish, related to rays
to glide along, as on ice or rollers, in the third person

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: the plural of the flatfish, and the verb for gliding on blades or wheels.

clue.text: As individuals, never interrupting in a contemptuous manner

indicators.note: one piece breaking into another and splitting it means one goes inside the other

parts.note: to act as individuals is to act one at a time, singly
ne'er is the poetic shortened form of never

explanation.surface: Someone notes that people never cut in rudely when they act one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' signals the poetic contraction ne'er breaking into the phrase for one at a time; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with a sneer means doing it with scorn, so the adverb describes contemptuous behaviour.

clue.text: See drunk keeping quiet

indicators.note: the drunk holds onto quiet, so that letter sits inside the word for him

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: An instruction to notice a drunk who is keeping his mouth shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, a plain synonym for seeing it.

clue.text: Hurried as journalist dedicated to his or her profession

parts.words: dedicated to his or her profession
parts.note: used before a noun, as in 'a career diplomat', career means devoted to one's working life
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Describes a journalist who rushed about, wholly devoted to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the journalist first, but ED goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along headlong, so the past tense means went at speed.

clue.text: German maybe in extreme circle

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, meaning excessive
a circle has the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Suggests a German person who belongs to some fringe group.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a typical German first name, so a German man might well be called it; 'maybe' shows it is an example.

clue.text: Doctor has year with a French practice

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: A doctor spends a year working in a French surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or trial run carried out before the real thing is a form of practice.

clue.text: It's clear GP's kit isn't bad for providing first-aid item

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad state and need to be set right into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient complains that their family doctor's medical kit is plainly inadequate.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder starts at 'clear', not 'It's'; 'isn't' supplies the N and the second I, S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive dressing put over a small cut is a basic item in any first-aid box.

clue.text: Short article in paper: 'Team faces ban'

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
to bar someone is to ban them

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a team being hit with a suspension.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism, a sidebar is a brief piece printed next to a main story.

clue.text: Fish around for someone to deal with health problem?

definitions.text: someone to deal with health problem?

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the fish is read from back to front

parts.note: the cod is a common sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone goes fishing for a person who can sort out a medical problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor is the person you consult about an illness; this is the informal short form.

clue.text: 'Globe-trotter' in London, say?

parts.note: the Globe is Shakespeare's playhouse in London, so a person who trots along to it is a playgoer

explanation.surface: Points to a world traveller visiting London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Globe-trotter' seems to mean a world traveller, but here the Globe is the theatre on London's South Bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who visits the Globe to see a play is a person who regularly attends plays.

clue.text: Politician participating in 'Strictly' dances

definitions.meaning: Ed ..., the former Labour minister, was famously a contestant on Strictly Come Dancing

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the dancing ex-minister is also the plural of a word for grand formal dances. Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC TV ballroom contest.

clue.text: Trendy translation making change to the usual order

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a version is a rendering of a text into another language

explanation.surface: A fashionable new translation reorders the original text.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning something upside down or reversing its normal sequence is the technical meaning of this noun.

clue.text: Entrance gets changed on the outside, having different colours

indicators.note: the word for changed wraps around the entrance

parts.note: varied means altered or changed
a gate is an entrance to a field or garden

explanation.surface: A garden gate is repainted on its outer side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves or petals with patches of more than one hue are described with this word.

clue.text: Men failing to work out who wrote spy stories

indicators.note: the letters must be worked out, reshaped into the right arrangement

explanation.surface: Men can't figure out the identity of the writer of spy thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: This British novelist created James Bond, the most famous spy in fiction.

clue.text: Very rich and very drunk?

definitions.meaning: ... drunk means so drunk you stagger about

explanation.definitionFit: The word is short for 'rolling in money' and also intensifies drunkenness in 'rolling drunk'.

clue.text: At home, understand about dog being unsettled

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for understand goes around the dog

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in 'I see'
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Staying in, someone finds their dog is nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is anxious and lacking in confidence feels unsettled.

clue.text: Tracks in zones of wood girl enters

indicators.note: the girl goes into the rings, so her name sits inside that word

parts.note: the growth rings of a tree are bands of wood
Di, short for Diana, is a stock crossword girl

explanation.surface: A girl walks into woodland along its paths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zones of wood' looks like a forest, but it means the growth rings in timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridings are paths for horse-riding, especially through woods, so they are tracks.

clue.text: Volunteers turning up, fathers going round — they may raise a laugh

indicators.note: the fathers encircle the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: sires are fathers, especially of animals

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers arrive while fathers mill about, all ready to entertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like arriving, but in a down clue it means reading upwards; 'going round' then puts the result inside the fathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Satires are works that mock their targets for comic effect, so they may raise a laugh.

clue.text: Pageboy possibly working this early?

indicators.note: the letters are worked over, set to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A young page is perhaps starting his duties at an early hour.
explanation.walkthrough: A pageboy here is not a young servant but a bob-length haircut with the ends turned under.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageboy is a kind of haircut, so it is an example of a hairdo; 'possibly' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Fair enough, one states, not revealing everything

indicators.note: only part of the words is shown, so the answer is hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Someone concedes a point but holds back part of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair enough' looks like one phrase, but only 'Fair' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair dealer is just and truthful, so fair and straight-dealing are synonyms here.

clue.text: Sea-girt location doesn't have owner-occupier

definitions.meaning: a small piece of land surrounded by sea
split as ..., a property that is rented out, so the owner does not live there

explanation.definitionFit: A small island is ringed by sea; read as two words the same letters say a property is rented.

clue.text: Chemical I love sufficed, needing energy

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
did means was enough, as in 'that did'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A speaker says love was enough for them, though they needed some energy.
explanation.definitionFit: An iodide is a compound of iodine with another element, so it is a chemical.

clue.text: New cabinet door — it has information written on it

definitions.text: it has information written on it

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters are rearranged into something different

explanation.surface: A newly fitted cupboard door has writing all over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A board in a hall or office for posting notices displays written information.

clue.text: Plumbing fixtures ejected liquid the wrong way

indicators.note: facing the wrong way means read backwards

parts.note: spat means spat out, ejected saliva

explanation.surface: Plumbing fittings sprayed water in the wrong direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Taps are fixtures that control water flow in a plumbing system.

clue.text: Deposit that is seen by river

definitions.meaning: to ... money is to deposit it
the sloping ground edging a river

explanation.definitionFit: One word both means put money away and names the raised edge along a river.

clue.text: Hurt girl having little lamb without tail

indicators.note: losing the tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Mary had a little lamb

explanation.surface: A girl is upset because her small lamb has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or damage it, a synonym for hurt.

clue.text: Managers put in — tenderness would be unusual

indicators.note: putting the letters in an unusual order means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Bosses who showed affection would be out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Supervisors in charge of an operation or building are the people who manage it.
